name: Win back churned customers from Stripe and HubSpot with Claude-written emails

parameters.content:
## Win back churned customers from Stripe and HubSpot with Claude-written emails

SaaS growth teams that never contact churned accounts again, even when the reason they left is fixed.

### How it works
Trigger: Weekly scan of churned accounts against triggers; release-notes webhook or a manual trigger when a feature ships; seasonal calendar for seasonal businesses.
1. Build the churned segment
2. Classify the reason
3. Match triggers to segments
4. Draft the message
5. Approve high-value sends
6. Send and route replies
7. Track reactivation
Every AI step is followed by a "Needs a person?" gate that parks low-confidence items; the write-back waits for an approval.

### Setup
1. Open "Config (edit me)" and fill in the fields (names, approver, quiet hours, thresholds).
2. Add credentials: Anthropic, plus Stripe / Chargebee + HubSpot, Gmail / Customer.io.
3. Run once with test_mode on, read the output, then switch the trigger on.

### Customization tips
Define the win-back triggers and the offer rules in the Config node; send through Customer.io or Gmail.
Guardrail to keep: Excluded segments (business closed, requested no contact, poor fit) never receive win-back messages.

Full blueprint: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/customer-win-back-automation/

## Trigger and config
The entry point and the one node you edit: names, approver, quiet hours, test mode.

## 1. Build the churned segment
Cancelled and lapsed accounts from billing and CRM with tenure, last plan, revenue, cancellation reason and any exit-survey text

## 2. Classify the reason
Exit reasons normalised into categories — price, missing feature, poor fit, switched to competitor, business closed, unresponsive — from the survey text and support history

## 3. Match triggers to segments
Rules: missing-feature churn waits for that feature to ship; price churn waits for a plan change or an annual-discount window; seasonal churn waits for the season; poor-fit and closed-business are excluded

## 4. Draft the message
A short, specific message referencing the reason they gave and the thing that changed, with one approved offer from the finance-owned set, in the account owner's voice

## 5. Approve high-value sends
Accounts above a revenue threshold pause for the owner's approval; the rest send automatically within the frequency cap

## 6. Send and route replies
Sent from the account owner; replies create a task for them with the account history; unsubscribes are honoured across all lists

## 7. Track reactivation
Reactivations matched to the message, segment, trigger and offer, so the rules and offers can be tuned quarterly

## Fill this in first
Every later node reads these values. Keep test_mode on for the first week.

nodes.notes:
Fill these in once; every later node reads them as $('Config (edit me)').item.json.config.*

test_mode = true: log what the workflow would write, without writing it, for the first week.
approval_mode = true: the approval node waits for a person; switch off per message type once it has earned it.

Also point the nodes at your own sources:
- Billing (cancellations, lapsed subscriptions)
- CRM and exit-survey text
- Release notes / product changelog
- Finance-approved offer set

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Draft the message" step of the Customer Win-Back Workflow workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: A short, specific message referencing the reason they gave and the thing that changed, with one approved offer from the finance-owned set, in the account owner's voice.

Rules:
- Excluded segments (business closed, requested no contact, poor fit) never receive win-back messages.
- One win-back message per account per quarter unless they reply.
- Offers come only from the approved set; the agent picks, it never invents a discount.
- High-value accounts require owner approval before sending.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.
